milestone.title: TUI Milestones lane: lifecycle column + lifecycle_at timestamp + drop legacy spec_status/execution_status display

intent.outcome: The raul TUI's Milestones lane shows the canonical M100 lifecycle (draft, groomed, approved, in-progress, done, self-reviewed, reviewed, complete, remediation, cancelled) as the status column instead of the legacy spec_status/execution_status strings, with a relative 'since' timestamp ('3d ago') showing when the milestone last transitioned. The row color is computed from effective_lifecycle() so it always reflects truth, even when legacy fields are stale. The data model gains a `lifecycle_at: Option<String>` field on MilestoneMeta (RFC3339 timestamp of the last lifecycle change) that every lifecycle transition sets, and a migration backfill ensures existing plans have a sensible value. Raul no longer reads the legacy spec_status / execution_status columns from mp JSON — those become write-side legacy bookkeeping only.

problem.description: Three coupled problems on the raul TUI's Milestones lane: (1) The status column shows legacy spec_status/execution_status strings ('ready', 'implemented', 'planned', 'done', etc.) which are the M100-pre-migration fields. The canonical state is now `lifecycle` (10 values), but the TUI displays the 6-string legacy set. A milestone with lifecycle='in-progress' may show 'ready' / 'planned' on the TUI because mp write paths don't always update the legacy fields in sync with the lifecycle field (effective_lifecycle derives lifecycle from legacy when the lifecycle field is the serde default, but write paths like set-execution-status only update lifecycle, not spec_status). (2) There is no timestamp showing when a milestone last changed status — users can't tell at a glance whether a milestone has been stuck in 'in-progress' for 1 day or 6 months. (3) The row color is computed from the legacy strings via progress::status_row_color(m.spec_status) and progress::status_row_color(m.execution_status), which can disagree with the canonical lifecycle. We need: (a) a single canonical source of truth in the model (lifecycle + lifecycle_at), (b) a parallel data-flow into raul that reads lifecycle instead of legacy fields, (c) a relative-time 'since' display.

in_scope: Add `lifecycle_at: Option<String>` field to MilestoneMeta (crates/mp-model/src/milestone.rs), `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`. Same pattern as `remediation_pre_state` so healthy milestones stay byte-identical in JSON shape goldens.

Set `lifecycle_at = Some(store::now_rfc3339())` at every site that writes `m.milestone.lifecycle = ...`: create_milestone (line 450), apply_spec_status (616), set_execution_status in-progress + done (863, 874), start-execution path (1725), complete (1799), reviews handoff → remediation (733, 742), remediation exit (824), show.rs:310 (if it's a real lifecycle write, otherwise exclude). Document each site with a brief comment explaining why this is a transition.

Migration backfill: in crates/mp/src/migrate.rs at every site that sets lifecycle (195, 753, 776, 810), also set lifecycle_at = Some(meta.created.clone()) so existing plans get a sensible 'since' value, not None.
Overlay flips (blocked, deferred, cancelled) do NOT update lifecycle_at — they're orthogonal. blocked_at is the existing field for 'blocked since'.
Bulk operations (milestone_bulk.rs apply_set_spec_status et al.) — same dual-write treatment in the loop.

Add `lifecycle: String` + `lifecycle_at: Option<String>` fields to raul::tui::app::MilestoneSummary (crates/raul/src/tui/app.rs:124). Remove `spec_status: String` + `execution_status: String` from MilestoneSummary — raul no longer reads those legacy columns. Note: BoardCard and AnnotationInfo still keep their legacy spec_status fields for now (different scope, separate work).
Update load_milestones in crates/raul/src/tui/runner.rs to populate the new fields from `m["lifecycle"]` and `m["lifecycle_at"]`.

Update the Milestones lane table in crates/raul/src/tui/render.rs (~line 999) to render lifecycle as the primary column and a relative 'since' string next to it. Drop the spec_status/execution_status columns (or fold them into a single secondary column if the user prefers; default: drop them entirely since they're stale).

Color the row by effective_lifecycle() via progress::status_row_color(m.lifecycle) — single source of truth. The existing role_table_is_exhaustive test in crates/raul/src/tui/progress.rs already covers the full lifecycle value set.

Tests: new file crates/raul/tests/tui_lifecycle_column.rs covering (a) Milestones table renders lifecycle as primary column, (b) 'since' shows relative time when lifecycle_at present and falls back to 'since updated' when None, (c) row color matches lifecycle, not legacy fields. Plus new mp-model unit tests pinning the lifecycle_at semantics: (d) every transition helper sets lifecycle_at, (e) overlay flips don't touch it, (f) migration backfill populates it. Plus a JSON-shape test that the new field appears only when set (skip_serializing_if honors).
out_of_scope: Dropping the legacy spec_status / execution_status fields from MilestoneMeta entirely — this milestone only stops READING them in the TUI. The fields stay on the data model (write paths keep dual-writing for now). A separate follow-up milestone (M145 in earlier discussion) drops the fields from the model and collapses effective_spec_status / effective_execution_status to shims over effective_lifecycle(). The M104 B-44 asymmetric-shape test (validate/plan.rs:615) gets removed in that follow-up.
Updating BoardCard.spec_status / AnnotationInfo.kind to use lifecycle — different scope (review/board surface).
The 'since updated' fallback showing a separate 'created' column — current TUI doesn't surface created_at; out of scope.

Per-state timestamps (e.g., how long has it been 'in-progress' specifically, separately from 'how long has it been approved') — would require a previous_lifecycle_at field. YAGNI for now; the git log via `mp milestone log` (M112 S4) covers detailed history.
Time-zone-aware display formatting — show relative time ('3d ago') only; no locale-specific formatting.

design_decisions.choice: RFC3339 (same as created, updated, blocked_at, archived_at)
design_decisions.rationale: Already established in the codebase (crates/mp/src/store.rs:759 now_rfc3339). Use the same helper at every site — no new dep, no format negotiation, no chrono::DateTime round-trip.
Mirrors remediation_pre_state (crates/mp-model/src/milestone.rs:125) which keeps healthy milestone JSON byte-identical to pre-change. Critical for the JSON shape goldens (M131 AC pattern).

design_decisions.choice: Lifecycle field changes only — overlay flips (blocked/deferred/cancelled) do NOT update lifecycle_at
design_decisions.rationale: lifecycle_at answers 'when did the milestone last move between lifecycle states'. Overlay flips are orthogonal and have their own timestamps (blocked_at). Mixing them would muddy the meaning.

We don't have the actual transition timestamp from pre-migration plans. created is the best honest approximation: it tells the user 'this milestone has been around since date X, and we're displaying its lifecycle value as of that creation'. Falls back gracefully — better than None (which the TUI would render as '?' or 'unknown').

design_decisions.choice: Drop spec_status and execution_status columns entirely from MilestoneSummary; show only lifecycle + since
design_decisions.rationale: The legacy fields are stale-by-design and the user explicitly chose to move past them. Showing both would clutter the row without adding signal. If anyone needs the legacy view, they can run `mp show <id>` which still emits both for backward compat.

design_decisions.choice: Relative time only ('3d ago', '2w ago', 'never') — no full timestamp in the row
design_decisions.rationale: Width budget on the lane table is tight (4-5 cols max). Full RFC3339 would truncate. Relative time is the highest-signal/lowest-space format for 'how long has it been stuck here'. Full timestamp available on detail view (`mp show <id>` shows lifecycle_at).
